comparison.scope: Four 9.98 s loaded seeds; retained local rates versus zero rates at identical deformation, each at three steps over20 ms. Sampled motion/contact changes, not continuous peaks, long-time decay, calibrated stability or a unique cause. Fixed boundary changes world kinetic energy. Source hashes collected before execution.

findings: All 24 short controls complete. Retained-rate and zero-rate loaded casings move with a stationary hub; rider/suspension feedback is unnecessary for this short-window activity.
Energy residuals decrease across the three steps. Contact switching and local trajectories do not uniformly converge; neither damping calibration nor long-term stability is established.
Zero local rates do not create equilibrium: loaded deformation and stored energy remain.

Native nodal-force moments and physical contact-point moments differ under blocked rotation. Preserve the difference and infer the clamp moment by angular balance; do not change dynamics or add work. Independent inverse-distance weighting predicts the difference within 1e-8 N m.
The sampled nodal/contact-point moment difference reaches 1.212014378583169 N m. Independent contact-weight reconstruction matches all 24 records within 4.439229760698493e-10 N m.

Full-front retained-rate fine/finest differences reach 0.04108349167369893 m/s in node-0 velocity and 28.619473552715192 N in vertical load; reduced energy residuals do not qualify full trajectory/load convergence.
next: Receive hosted worker records and actual captures; quantify longer isolated decay/refinement before constitutive damping. Whole-bike perturbation recovery, 60 s idle and support-aware rider/IK remain open.
